name: Work Permit (Employee)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an employment contract signed by both employee and employer.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a qualifying job offer from a Swedish employer.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a monthly salary of at least SEK 34,470 (90% of the median salary published by Statistics Sweden, effective June 2026), also meeting any higher collective-agreement or profession-specific standard. Certain professions qualify at a reduced 75% threshold (SEK 28,725).

Employer must secure health, life, industrial injuries, and occupational pension insurance by the applicant's start date (or, for positions of 1 year or less, health insurance covering urgent/other medical care for the full stay).

outcome.duration_length: Maximum 2 years per grant (limited also by contract term and passport validity), renewable
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: Must have worked in Sweden for 4 of the past 7 years, maintaining permit conditions throughout, to reach permanent residence.

sources.title: Swedish Migration Agency -- Apply for a work permit in Sweden: SEK 34,470/month salary threshold (90% of median, effective June 2026), employer insurance, 2-year maximum duration
Swedish Migration Agency -- Apply for an extension of a work permit: confirms 4 years of work permit held, worked 4 of the past 7 years, as the threshold for permanent residence eligibility

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sweden). The SEK 34,470 salary threshold is very recent (effective June 2026, up from a lower pre-2026 figure) -- part of a broader tightening wave across Swedish migration law this year, alongside the citizenship reform (see se_naturalisation.json) and the asylum permanent-residence abolition (see se_international_protection.json). citizenship_after_months (96) is a chained estimate: 48 months to permanent residence eligibility on this route, plus Sweden's new standard 8-year (96-month) naturalization residence bar (see se_naturalisation.json) counted from the start of habitual residence generally -- these two clocks substantially overlap rather than stack sequentially in practice, so 96 months (matching the naturalization bar alone) is used as the more accurate total rather than a literal 48+96 sum.
